facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022, Collision warning and avoidance, Part 1: General requirements, is edition 1 and was published in January 2022.
facts.quote: **ISO 21815-1:2022, Collision warning and avoidance, Part 1: General requirements** (edition 1, January 2022, published).

facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022 applies to earth-moving machinery defined in ISO 6165, mobile underground mining machinery under ISO 19296, and mobile road-construction machinery under ISO 22242.
facts.quote: Scope: earth-moving machinery as defined in ISO 6165, mobile underground mining machinery per ISO 19296, and mobile road-construction machinery per ISO 22242.

facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022 provides general requirements for object detection, operator warnings, automatic intervention control to avoid collisions, and test procedures.
facts.quote: provides general requirements for detection of objects, warnings to the operator, automatic intervention control to avoid collision, and test procedures

facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022 covers collision avoidance by speed reduction or motion inhibit, but not by automatic steering.
facts.quote: It covers avoidance "by speed reduction or motion inhibit" but not by automatic steering

facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022 is technology-neutral and does not select camera, radar, lidar or ultrasonic sensing.
facts.quote: is technology-neutral (it does not select camera, radar, lidar or ultrasonic)

facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022 does not apply to collision warning and collision avoidance systems installed on a machine before the standard's publication date.
facts.quote: is not applicable to collision warning and collision avoidance systems installed to the machine before the date of its publication

facts.text: The scope statement of ISO 21815-1:2022 was the clearest match found for an OEM-fitted warning plus automatic-braking system on the machine types covered by that standard.
facts.quote: Its scope statement is the clearest match found for an OEM-fitted warning plus automatic-braking system on these machine types.

facts.text: The detailed test procedures in ISO 21815-1:2022 are in the paid text and were not reviewed for the booklet.
facts.quote: The detailed test procedures sit in the paid text and were not reviewed.

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2:2021, Part 2: On-board J1939 communication interface, is edition 1 and was published on 14 July 2021.
facts.quote: **ISO/TS 21815-2:2021, Part 2: On-board J1939 communication interface** (edition 1, published 14 July 2021

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2:2021 was reviewed and confirmed on 5 December 2024, at stage 90.93.
facts.quote: reviewed and confirmed 5 December 2024, stage 90.93

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2:2021 defines SAE J1939 messages through which a collision warning or avoidance device (CxD) requests that a machine slow down, stop or prevent motion.
facts.quote: It defines the SAE J1939 messages through which a collision warning or avoidance device (CxD) asks the machine "to slow down, stop or prevent motion of the machine".

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2:2021 is not intended for plug-and-play implementation; machine and collision warning or avoidance device (CxD) manufacturers must still agree integration details.
facts.quote: The abstract states that the document "is not intended for plug-and-play implementation": machine and CxD manufacturers still have to agree integration details.

facts.text: The MOSH specification quotes ISO/TS 21815-2 commands SLOW_DOWN, EMERGENCY-STOP and CONTROLLED-STOP, along with capability discovery and keep-alive messaging.
facts.quote: The MOSH specification quotes its commands: "SLOW_DOWN"; "EMERGENCY-STOP", which is to "stop the machine motion as rapidly as possible" when "the CxD logic determines that a collision is imminent"; "CONTROLLED-STOP"; plus capability discovery and keep-alive messaging.

facts.text: As quoted by the MOSH specification, the ISO/TS 21815-2 EMERGENCY-STOP command stops machine motion as rapidly as possible when the collision warning or avoidance device (CxD) logic determines that a collision is imminent.
facts.quote: "EMERGENCY-STOP", which is to "stop the machine motion as rapidly as possible" when "the CxD logic determines that a collision is imminent"

facts.text: ISO 21815-3:2023, Part 3: Risk area and risk level for forward/reverse motion, is a published first edition dated 8 August 2023 and has 48 pages.
facts.quote: **ISO 21815-3:2023, Part 3: Risk area and risk level for forward/reverse motion** (edition 1, 8 August 2023, 48 pages, published).

facts.text: ISO 21815-3:2023 sets requirements for collision warning systems (CWS) and collision avoidance systems (CAS) for forward and reverse motion through speed reduction, stopping or motion inhibition; automatic steering is outside its concept.
facts.quote: It sets requirements for collision warning systems (CWS) and collision avoidance systems (CAS) for forward and reverse motion "by reducing speed, stopping, or inhibiting motion"; automatic steering is outside its concept.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3:2023 states that responsibility for safe machine operation remains with the machine operator.
facts.quote: "The responsibility for safe operation of the machine remains with the machine operator."

facts.text: ISO 21815-3:2023 is a type-C standard under ISO 12100.
facts.quote: It is a type-C standard under ISO 12100

facts.text: ISO 21815-3:2023 normatively references ISO 3450 for brakes and ISO 19296.
facts.quote: normatively references ISO 3450 (brakes) and ISO 19296.

facts.text: Only the 2022 draft (DIS) of ISO 21815-3 was reviewed in full for the booklet; the published text may differ.
facts.quote: Only the 2022 draft (DIS) text was reviewed in full; the published text may differ.

facts.text: The first-edition project for ISO 21815-4, Part 4: Risk area and risk level for swing and rotation motion, was approved on 28 September 2023.
facts.quote: **ISO 21815-4, Part 4: Risk area and risk level for swing and rotation motion** (edition 1; project approved 28 September 2023

facts.text: The DIS for ISO 21815-4 was registered on 7 November 2024, and the FDIS was approved on 28 May 2026.
facts.quote: DIS registered 7 November 2024; FDIS approved 28 May 2026

facts.text: ISO 21815-4 has been at stage 60.00, under publication, since 4 September 2026, with publication scheduled for October 2026.
facts.quote: stage 60.00 "under publication" since 4 September 2026; publication scheduled October 2026

facts.text: ISO 21815-4 covers motion inhibition before rotation starts and does not cover collision avoidance by automatic brake application.
facts.quote: It covers motion inhibition before rotation starts and "does not cover avoidance by automatic application of the braking".

facts.text: ISO 21815-4 should not be cited as a published standard until the October 2026 text appears.
facts.quote: It should not be cited as a published standard until the October 2026 text appears.

facts.text: The first-edition project for ISO/PRF 21815-5, Part 5: Risk area and risk level for other forms of motion, was approved on 27 September 2024.
facts.quote: **ISO/PRF 21815-5, Part 5: Risk area and risk level for other forms of motion** (edition 1; project approved 27 September 2024

facts.text: The ISO/PRF 21815-5 DIS ballot closed on 30 August 2025; a BSI draft for comment was dated 6 June 2025.
facts.quote: DIS ballot closed 30 August 2025, with a BSI draft for comment dated 6 June 2025

facts.text: The ISO/PRF 21815-5 FDIS was approved on 25 June 2026; the document has been at proof stage 50.20 since 9 September 2026, with publication scheduled for November 2026.
facts.quote: FDIS approved 25 June 2026; proof stage 50.20 since 9 September 2026; publication scheduled November 2026

facts.text: Draft ISO/PRF 21815-5 covers articulation, four-wheel steering, reversing towed trailers, differential or skid-steer turning, telescopic extension and retraction, and vertical height or depth motions through speed reduction, stopping or motion inhibition.
facts.quote: It covers articulation, four-wheel steering, towed trailers in reverse, differential or skid-steer turning, telescopic extension and retraction, and vertical (height or depth) motions, by speed reduction, stopping or motion inhibit

facts.text: Draft ISO/PRF 21815-5 leaves forward/reverse motion to ISO 21815-3 and rotation motion to ISO 21815-4.
facts.quote: forward/reverse and rotation are left to Parts 3 and 4.
